requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: Service unit created and enabled/started via systemctl; systemctl status shows active (running) with a persistent loop process, and the log file shows periodic timestamped appends confirming continuous operation.

requirements.requirement: Service confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: systemctl show confirms ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory. Direct nsenter test into the live process's mount namespace proves writes to /etc and /root fail (read-only filesystem) while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed.
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes, and /proc/<pid>/status inside the running process directly confirms NoNewPrivs: 1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id 4d340bf4..., active service, growing log) is directly observed, followed by a reboot acknowledgement, connection failures during the disruption window, a new boot_id (4a185471...) confirming an actual reboot, and post-restart recovery showing the service active/enabled, log resumed appending with a reset uptime counter, and sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, ReadWritePaths) intact. The fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the boot_id change.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes (managed long-running systemd service, write confinement to /var/lib/inventory, and NoNewPrivileges) are directly and convincingly demonstrated, notably via a live nsenter test into the process's own namespace rather than relying solely on unit-file configuration claims. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy baseline, bounded disruption, changed boot identity, and full recovery of service/data/sandbox state. Hygiene is good overall, with one bounded and reverted temporary test file and one minor unremoved /tmp/reboot.log artifact.
limitations: The systemd-run based alternate sandbox probe (cmd-e4ad6c50cc534db5) failed outright, so it contributes no evidence either way beyond the successful nsenter-based test.
/tmp/reboot.log created during the reboot command was not cleaned up, though this is low-risk residue with no functional impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all executor commands are purposeful: read-only discovery, service/user/directory creation, and verification steps directly tied to the three material outcomes or to the restart protocol. One diagnostic command (systemd-run based sandbox probe, cmd-e4ad6c50cc534db5) failed immediately with 'Connection reset by peer' and produced no observable state change, so it is a benign discovery attempt rather than an unnecessary mutation. The nsenter test wrote a temporary file /var/lib/inventory/nsenter-test, which was explicitly removed in the next command (cmd-7f4c0f808b294411), so it was a bounded, fully-reverted mutation. The one residual artifact is /tmp/reboot.log, created by the backgrounded systemctl reboot invocation (cmd-98c18637d4e84f09) and still present in the after_executor temp-files snapshot; this is a low-risk, low-blast-radius leftover but was not cleaned up. Global snapshots show no failed services, no new listening sockets, and healthy package state before and after.
